To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we found a protein similar to BjI (a protein that specifically inhibits the clotting activity of thrombin) in the plasma of three different species, Bothrops alternata, B. jararacussus and C. durissus terrificu.
the presence of BjIs in the plasas of B. alternatus, B. jararacussus and C. d. terrificus snakes was demonstrated, and that these proteins are immunologically related to the BjI from B. jaracara.

we identified proteins similar to B. jararacaa coagulation inhibitor in the plasma of three different species (B. alternatus, B. jarararacussu, and C. durissus terrificuss) of vipers, suggesting that this inhibitor is widely distributed in Crotalinae species in Brazil.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the isolation and characterization of BjI-like molecules from the plasma of B. alternatus, B. jararacussus and C. durissus terrifics snakes.
the characterization of a new group of proteins with coagulant-inhibitory activity that is present in the plasma of snakes.
the identification and characterization of a novel group of snake plasma proteins that are similar to the BjI and that are widely distributed in Brazilian snakes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
BjI-like inhibitors are widely distributed in Crotalinae species.
these proteins may represent a new class of inhibitors that could be found in many different animal species.
the presence of BjIs in snake plasma is related to a specific inhibition of the coagulant action of thrombin.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the presence of BjIs in snake plasmas is a characteristic of Crotalinae species.

BjI is a protein that is present in the plasma of many snakes and that its presence is related to a prolongation of the thrombin time, which is a parameter that is widely used for the evaluation of the coagulation process in the blood.
the BjI-like protein is a member of a family of proteins that is present in the plasma of many snake species.
The main takeaway from our work is that
BjI is present in all three species tested.
BjI-like protein is a common feature in Brazilian Crotalinae plasmas, and it is likely that this is the case in other species of snakes.
the coagulant inhibitors of the plasma of snakes of the family Crotalinae are similar to BjI and that these inhibitors are widely distributed among these snakes.
